red.brief: Gravelly middle-aged man, a 1940s film-noir private eye. Low smoky voice, dry and world-weary, slow deliberate delivery, American.
red.line: The way I see it, somebody in this room poisoned that drink. I saw Duke at the bar, right before. Case closed... unless one of you wants to talk.

mint.brief: Crisp, slightly nasal upper-class British woman in her thirties. Condescending and precise, fast and articulate, smug.
mint.line: Obviously it was Lola. Let me explain this slowly, since nobody else was paying attention. She said the bar. I saw her on the casino floor. Keep up.

biscuit.brief: Warm drawling Texan man in his fifties. Deep and friendly, relaxed cowboy cadence, a little raspy.
biscuit.line: Now hold your horses, partner. I was over at the dice game the whole night. I ain't never killed nothin' but a steak, and that's a fact.

lola.brief: Bubbly young woman in her twenties with a valley-girl lilt. Fast, breathy and dramatic, loves gossip, American.
lola.line: Okay so, not to be dramatic, but I literally SAW Pip fiddle with the slot machine. Like, I screamed inside. Everyone knows it's Pip. Everyone.

duke.brief: Pompous man in his forties with a theatrical courtroom voice. Over-enunciated, self-important, mid-Atlantic accent.
duke.line: Objection! Hearsay! Let the record show I was at the roulette table, and I have witnesses. Probably. The defense rests, your honor. I mean, everyone.

pip.brief: Smooth confident man in his thirties, a slick Las Vegas high roller. Charming, quick-talking, New York accent.
pip.line: Odds are, it's Ozzie. I'd bet the whole house on it. Me? I was on a hot streak at blackjack, making this crew money. Check the bank, sweetheart.

coco.brief: Sweet elderly woman in her eighties, warm and a little shaky. A Southern American grandmother, kind but sharp.
coco.line: Oh, dearie. I may be old, but I saw Mint shove that poor boy into the duck pond. Shame on you, Mint. Lord have mercy. Now somebody eat something.

ozzie.brief: Loud hot-tempered man in his thirties with a gruff Boston accent. Shouty, impatient, quick to explode.
ozzie.line: Are you KIDDING me?! ME?! I was at the slots the whole damn time! Say that again, I dare you! You're all gonna regret this, I swear!

teal.brief: Young nervous person in their early twenties, light and uncertain voice, lots of upspeak, polite and a bit lost.
teal.line: Uh, sorry, first time here? I think I saw Snow near the snack bowl? Like, I definitely did. I think. Is that how this works? Should I vote?

snow.brief: Tipsy cheerful woman in her forties, slurring slightly, giggly, husky voice with sloppy timing.
snow.line: Okay, okay, okay. Lissen. I saw Red do the thing. With the... the knife. There was only one Red. I counted. Who's buying the next round?

moss.brief: Paranoid man in his fifties. An intense raspy voice that drops to a whisper, then bursts into fast jittery rants.
moss.line: Wake up, people. The pretzels, the chandelier, the cameras. It's all connected. The house is in on it. Voting is exactly what they want us to do.

ruby.brief: Gentle warm woman in her thirties, soft-spoken and caring, sincere, with a slight Irish lilt.
ruby.line: Oh, sweetie. I hate saying this, I really do, but I saw Biscuit near the bar right before. I'm so sorry, Biscuit. Please tell us where you were.

sky.brief: Anxious young man with a high trembling voice, stammering and breathless, always on the edge of panic.
sky.line: I-I s-saw it! Coco messed with the chandelier chain, and then it just... it FELL! I'm not crazy! Oh no, oh no. Can we please go home now?

peach.brief: Passionate Italian chef, a man in his forties with a big expressive voice, a strong Italian accent and theatrical gestures.
peach.line: Mamma mia. Something smells off, and it is not my kitchen. Your alibi is half-baked, Ink. Raw in the middle. I vote you. Chef's kiss.

ink.brief: Laid-back young man with a mellow low voice and a slow, chill Californian surfer cadence.
ink.line: Bro. Real talk. I had my headphones on the whole time, vibing at the bar. Wasn't me. But Lime? The energy's off. Not the vibe, man.

lime.brief: Quick-witted woman in her thirties, a stand-up comedian with a sardonic raspy New York voice and punchy timing.
lime.line: Tough crowd. So a killer walks into a casino... and nobody notices, apparently. Look, I was at Plinko, losing money. Which is the real crime here.

croupier.brief: Elegant French croupier, a man in his fifties. Refined, calm and measured, formal, with a French accent.
croupier.line: Place your bets, ladies and gentlemen. Place your bets. No more bets. Seventeen, black, odd. Congratulations to the gentleman in the fedora.

dealer.brief: Professional casino dealer, a woman in her thirties with a clear friendly voice. Efficient and upbeat, American.
dealer.line: Cards are out. Dealer shows a six. Fifteen for you, sir. Hit or stand? Twenty-one! Blackjack pays three to two. Nice hand, nice hand.

announcer.brief: Excited old-time horse-race announcer, a man with fast rapid-fire commentary, high energy, a classic radio sound.
announcer.line: And they're off! Quackers takes the early lead, Sir Waddles on the outside, here comes Duckie Brown down the stretch, it's neck and neck, it's QUACKERS by a beak!

pa.brief: Smooth casino PA announcer with a deep velvety male voice. Warm, unhurried, a lounge host.
pa.line: Good evening, and welcome to Last Call. The tables are open, the drinks are on the house, and the house always wins. Please, enjoy your stay.

bartender.brief: Friendly gruff bartender, a woman in her forties with a husky voice. Wry, unflappable, Brooklyn accent.
bartender.line: What'll it be, hon? Martini, beer, whiskey? Somebody already sent you one, on the house. No, I didn't see who. I don't see nothin'. Drink up.
